newsitem.title: USA: Columbia reorganization won't stop probe-WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Columbia reorganization won't stop probe-WSJ.

text.p: The change in leadership at Columbia/HCA Healthcare Corp will not slow down the federal investigation into its billing practices, but it could help to minimize its exposure to civil and criminal penalties if it is charged with wrongdoing, The Wall Street Journal said.
In Wednesday's electronic edition, the paper quoted a law enforcement official as saying the company's personnel decisions had no bearing on the investigation.

The paper also quoted legal experts as saying that the recent resignation of Columbia's two top officials, plus the abandonment of the company's more controversial practices could give it a little bit of leverage in a settlement negotiation.
One sentencing guideline provision calls for the reduction of potential fines if the company demonstrates that it has taken steps to rectify past indiscretions, the article said.
Columbia facilities in at least seven states are being probed for possible Medicare and Medicaid fraud.
